body: TPG offloads 40 lakh Shadowfax shares worth Rs 113.6 crore amid a sharp rise in the logistics firm’s stock and improving financial performanceTPG, Shadowfax, NewQuest Asia Fund IV, bulk deal, block deal, stake sale, PE firm, private equity, logistics, ecommerce, quick commerce, D2C, Abhishek Bansal, Vaibhav Khandelwal, BSE, FY27, revenue growth, net profit, dark stores, stock marketPrivate equity (PE) major TPG has offloaded more shares of listed logistics company Shadowfax Technologies through an open-market transaction worth Rs 113.6 crore.According to BSE data, TPG, through its entity NewQuest Asia Fund IV (Singapore), sold 40 lakh shares of Shadowfax at Rs 284.03 apiece. The identity of the buyer was not disclosed.The transaction was executed at a premium of 1.3 per cent to the company’s closing share price on Wednesday.This is the third major stake sale by TPG in Shadowfax over the past three months. In September, the PE firm sold shares worth Rs 200 crore, while in August it offloaded shares worth Rs 300 crore through a block deal. With the latest transaction, TPG has sold Shadowfax shares worth nearly Rs 614 crore across three deals since August.The latest sale comes as Shadowfax’s share price has recorded a sharp rise in recent months. The stock touched an all-time high of Rs 291.90 on 24 September. It has gained 14.22 per cent over the past month and more than 143.97 per cent in the last six months.The rally has coincided with an improvement in the company’s financial performance. Shadowfax reported an eight-fold year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 65.4 crore in the first quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 8 crore in the year-ago period.Operating revenue rose 65 per cent year-on-year and 10 per cent quarter-on-quarter to Rs 1,358.1 crore in the quarter ended June 2026.Following the quarterly results, Shadowfax raised its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 38-40 per cent from the earlier projection of 28-30 per cent.Founded in 2015 by Abhishek Bansal and Vaibhav Khandelwal, Shadowfax operates a logistics network serving e-commerce, quick commerce and direct-to-consumer brands. The company was listed on the stock exchanges earlier this year.Shadowfax currently operates across more than 16,372 pincodes and plans to increase its dark-store network from 47 to 100 by March 2027 as it expands its quick commerce operations.Shares of Shadowfax closed Wednesday’s trading session 0.09 per cent lower at Rs 280.50 on the BSE.
